---
title: "Glossary"
guide-section: "Understanding replaylab"
---

The vocabulary used in the code and documentation.

# The game

**pool** ([`DesignPool`](../reference/datasets.pool.DesignPool.qmd))
: The designs of one game: one target, one split. What an agent may buy from.
  It carries only the visible features; cluster ids and outcomes ride along
  hidden, and nothing hands the object itself to an agent.

**game / campaign**
: A *game* is the static configuration (target, split, rounds, batch size,
  budget, and delay, encapsulated in [`GameConfig`](../reference/config.GameConfig.qmd)). 
  A *campaign* is one play of it against the
  [`CampaignStore`](../reference/store.CampaignStore.qmd).

**alias**
: Agents never see real design ids, only `d0001`-style aliases. The mapping is
  built by sorting real ids on `sha256(f"{seed}|{id}")` and reshuffled by every
  seed: a per-episode pseudonym, not a naming scheme. A real id is a stable
  handle on the whole dataset -- anything holding one can join it to outside
  knowledge or to an earlier run's transcript -- while an alias points at
  nothing outside its own campaign, and two seeds cannot be lined up on
  `d0001`. It is deterministic (no random generator), so one seed reproduces
  the same mapping on any machine. **Consequence:** state keyed by alias
  belongs to exactly one seed, which is why policies are built fresh per seed.

**round, tick, clock**
: Rounds are *batch slots*. `state.clock` counts elapsed rounds. `Campaign.submit`
  creates a batch, hands it to the backend, ingests what is ready, then ticks
  once. A batch submitted at clock *t* with delay *d* delivers at *t + d*.
  `Campaign.wait` (tick without buying any batch) is allowed only while something is pending.

**batch**
: Designs proposed or submitted together, moving only forward through state transitions
  `proposed → submitted → partial → complete`.

# Status of a design

| Term | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| **purchased** | in a batch that left `proposed` (delivered *or* pending) |
| **delivered** | outcome has arrived and is in the store |
| **pending** | purchased but outcome has not arrived yet |
| **unpurchased** | still available to buy |

# Outcomes

**hit**
: any binding record for the (design, target) pair is True. An *inconclusive*
  result (`hit is None`) is a purchase but not a hit, and is excluded from
  model fitting.

**conflict / strength / kd_molar**
: conflicting binding records; the strongest label (Strong/Medium/Weak); the
  smallest KD converted to molar units.

**budget**
: `rounds × batch_size`: upper bound on the total number of designs that can be bought 
  during a campaign.

# The agent side

**snapshot** ([`CampaignState`](../reference/domain.CampaignState.qmd))
: Immutable view of a campaign accessible to a policy or advisor function: 
  designs, batches, delivered outcomes, clock, and derived views (`unpurchased_ids`,
  `budget_remaining`, …). Everything the agent knows comes through this object.

**feature orientation**
: Feature values stay *raw* in the pool (a lower-is-better ProteinMPNN score
  looks lower); the ±1 orientation is applied once inside
  [`Preprocessor`](../reference/advisor.preprocess.Preprocessor.qmd), so every
  covariate points the same way before the model sees it. The direction is
  declared once per target in `config/features.yaml` (`higher_is_better`), and
  that declaration is also what every *raw* sort reads: round 1's
  `first_column`, the fallback, and `fixed:<metric>`. It is a statement of
  which way is good, not a modelling trick -- the model would learn the sign by
  itself -- but with it declared, a positive weight reads as "better, more
  hits" and nothing sorts a metric the wrong way.

**policy**
: `choose(state, k, rng) -> ids` returns a batch proposal given the current campaign state. 
  Returns `[]` to mean *stop*. 
  The baseline policies are: `random`, `fixed:<metric>`, `learner`, `learner_sim`;
  each can be optionally wrapped in `WithStop`.

**stop rules**
: Advice on when to stop the campaign, evaluated at round boundaries on delivered purchases only.
  `low_yield` (the default): fires from 20 purchases when the cumulative hit
  rate is below 0.03.

**frozen configuration**
: `config/frozen_v1.yaml` pins the model hyper-parameters chosen on `N-dev`
  only.

# Splits and evaluation

**cluster** (a family)
: Designs grouped by 3-mer cosine distance ≤ 0.4 -- the connected components of
  that pair graph, built once by `data/build_clusters.py`. Hidden from every
  policy and every tool. It does two jobs: keeping a family whole when the
  folds are cut, and scoring campaigns by `distinct_families`.

**fold**
: One of three groups a target's designs are split into, with
  `StratifiedGroupKFold` on the cluster as *group* (a family never straddles a
  fold) and the hit as *label* (equal hit rates), taking the first seed that
  lands every fold within ±2 designs and ±2 hits. **Fold 2 is the held-out
  fold.** Frozen in `data/splits/folds.csv`.

**dev / held-out split**
: `dev` is folds 0 and 1 (`N-dev` and the other development games), `heldout`
  is fold 2 (`N-held`), `all` ignores folds. Held-out outcomes can only be read
  with `final_run=True`, the evaluation runner refuses held-out games entirely,
  and `replaylab serve` exits with code 2 for them.

**replay vs live**
: `mode="replay"` plays recorded outcomes through the
  [`ReplayBackend`](../reference/backends.ReplayBackend.qmd); `mode="live"`
  will drive a real campaign through the pinned OpenAPI spec.
  Both implement the same three-method `LabBackend` interface.
